title: Take one terminal block off a wired DIN-rail strip in a control panel with a screwdriver
instruction: Take the blue terminal block off the DIN rail with the screwdriver and put it in the tray, and leave the beige blocks where they are.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111, about 0.8M US workers) and electrical equipment assemblers (51-2028) take single blocks off wired terminal strips when control panels are modified. The latch is released with a flat screwdriver in the slot at the block's foot, between ducts and wired neighbours, without loosening those neighbours.
setup: A control panel's steel mounting plate (galvanised, 240 x 280 x 2.5 mm) lies flat on the table, as panel builders wire it, its centre 0.305 m in front of the arm bases and 0.04 m right of their midline. On it: a steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail (240 mm), screwed down, left to right, its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases; a grey PVC slotted wiring duct (40 x 40 mm, 280 mm long, lid on) along each side of the rail, 30 mm from the block ends. On the rail between two zinc end brackets: 15 polyamide push-in terminal blocks (6.2 mm thick along the rail, 72.4 mm long across it with the release tab, 36 mm tall, 9.5 g; dimensions and build files in the README): the blue one 2 cm right of the rail's centre, a beige block 10 mm from each of its faces, and beyond each beige block 6 more beige blocks packed 0.2 mm apart. Each beige block has a black 1.5 mm2 PVC wire (3.0 mm) in each end, running straight into the duct on that side; the blue block's wires are already disconnected. Each block has a rigid hook under the far lip and a sprung foot (1.0 N/mm) under the near lip, opened through a 2.4 x 4.8 mm release slot at its near end. A flat-blade screwdriver (blade 4.0 x 0.8 mm, 75 mm, 60 g) stands handle up in a black plastic holder (40 x 40 x 50 mm), 0.16 m in front of the arm bases and 0.08 m left of their midline. An empty black plastic tray (inside 170 x 64 mm, walls 3 mm thick and 12 mm high), its centre 0.18 m in front of the arm bases and 0.225 m right of their midline.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the blue block is released (the gripper open and not touching it) and resting still on the tray's floor (its lowest point within 2 mm of the floor) for 1 s, with the two beige blocks beside it undisturbed (still latched and within 1 mm of where they started along the rail); 0.75 in the tray (centre inside its inner walls, lowest point below their tops), released or still held; 0.5 off the rail (base 20 mm or more above the lips, or centre outside the rail's footprint); 0.25 its sprung foot released (its tooth 2.0 mm or more out past its latched position, measured against the rail, or the near end lifted 6.5 mm or more off the lip); else 0 (a shifted or tipped block still latched scores 0). Capped at 0.25 if a beige block was disturbed.
reset_notes: Put the blue block back in its place: hook its far end under the far lip, then press its near end down until the sprung foot clicks. Stand the screwdriver back in its holder, handle up. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, GPU. Block of this task's own design, printable (build files in the README): rigid hook; sprung foot as a 1 N/mm slider (2.0 N at release) opened through a 2.4 mm slot. Collision boxes and convex pieces; contact offset 0.2 mm. Rail lips 2 mm (1 mm real; the printed teeth sit 1 mm higher). Wires are fixed straight 3 mm rods. Release read from the robot's contact force on the block.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; the screwdriver stayed in its holder, the blue block latched); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 965); held in the tray: 0.75; lifted off the rail and held: 0.5; foot levered out and held: 0.25; same motions without the screwdriver: 0.0
